checks_run.expected: R1 -> 'imports package node:test'; R2 -> 'module loader via process.execve'; architecture.test.ts 80/80; real tree 0 violations
checks_run.actual: R1 1 violation 'imports package node:test'; bare `test` 1; R2 1 'module loader via process.execve'; (process as any).execve 1; globalThis.process.execve 1; import {execve} from node:process 1. architecture.test.ts 80/80 (90/90 with the 10 probe tests), including the R1/R2 self-checks at architecture.test.ts:351/357 and P12/X6-X8/A1. Real tree: 0 violations.

checks_run.procedure: Independently enumerate Node 22 builtinModules, node:-only built-ins and every own or inherited process.* key, and classify each as a loader/exec route. Probe any open candidate in the lint and at runtime
checks_run.command: node -e '<builtinModules + process key walk>'; node r3.mjs (SIGUSR1 -> inspector -> Runtime.evaluate); node r4.mjs (_debugProcess); node --disable-sigusr1 r3.mjs/r4.mjs
checks_run.environment: disposable dir $TMPDIR/insp outside the repo; node v22.22.2; loopback only
checks_run.expected: Every reachable loader/exec route is banned or is a stated residual (future/unknown built-in, WebAssembly/node:wasi)
checks_run.actual: This does not hold. process.kill(process.pid,'SIGUSR1') and process._debugProcess(process.pid) start the inspector without importing node:inspector. Global fetch + WebSocket + Runtime.evaluate then runs child_process (output 'uid=0(root)'). The lint reports 0 violations for both (N1/N2). Production runs node without --disable-sigusr1, and that flag closes the route. Every other built-in and process.* member is banned, a stated residual, or not a loader. Raised as F-DG1-129 (Low, non-mandatory).

summary: PASS. F-DG1-128 is CLOSED_VERIFIED: node:test and process.execve are both caught, architecture.test.ts passes 80/80, and the real tree has 0 violations. Every required check ran green except two BLOCKED for missing tools: installer AC-1 (effect) and the real-repo install (no registry), and the Node 24 sweep (no binary). D-054's exhaustiveness claim for Node 22 does not hold: SIGUSR1 / process._debugProcess starts the inspector, and arbitrary code then runs via Runtime.evaluate. This is raised as new Low, non-mandatory F-DG1-129. No Critical, High or mandatory finding is open.
